title: Scarlet Hammer — Fast-Fashion Flash Sale
description: A blunt two-column retail blaster where a wall-sized compressed percentage dominates the left half and a stark black price-tag rectangle anchors the right — all on an unbroken red field. No gradients, no softness, just the flat typographic aggression of H&M and Zara email campaigns.
philosophy: This slide exists to stop a scroll in under one second, the same way a sale sticker slapped on a storefront window does. It treats typographic scale and hard flat color as the only tools that matter, deliberately refusing texture, photography, or visual breathing room. It is made for brands that have a single message and zero tolerance for hesitation. Nuance is rejected as waste; urgency is the entire product.
goodFor: Seasonal discount announcements and Black Friday campaign decks
Fast-fashion email hero banner mockups presented to creative directors
Social media story slides for retail brand promotions
avoidFor: B2B SaaS investor pitch decks or Series A fundraising
Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews with dense data
Luxury or premium brand positioning presentations
Academic conference papers or policy briefing slides
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Retail brutalism at full volume — the slide should feel like a sale sticker slapped onto a storefront window and blown up to fill an entire screen. Composition is confrontational and bifurcated: an overwhelming typographic mass dominates one side while a hard-edged identity block anchors the other, creating tension with no resolution. The mood is fast-fashion urgency distilled to its most aggressive form — a visual countdown with no softness allowed. Avoid all texture, gradients, decorative elements, or compositional breathing room; the discomfort of zero negative space is intentional and load-bearing.

examples.layoutNotes: Hard 50/50 two-column split, edge-to-edge bleed with zero outer margin on all sides. Left column is consumed entirely by an oversized compressed sale percentage that clips at both the top and bottom edges, functioning as a flat typographic wall rather than a text element. Right column holds a hard-blocked dark rectangle — the price-tag unit — vertically centered within its half, containing the brand or sale name as a tight counter-label. Hierarchy is achieved through scale violence alone: one enormous mark against one contained label, with nothing permitted in between.

examples.promptCore: A flat retail assault: two hard slabs of color collide at center stage — the dominant left field screams a single promotional truth at maximum typographic scale, while the black right block delivers the supporting payload in compressed staccato lines. The mood is H&M storefront glass and Zara email blast — zero softness, zero texture, zero hesitation. Composition is bluntly asymmetric and scale alone carries all hierarchy. Avoid gradients, illustrative elements, iconography, or any visual cushioning that lets the eye slow down.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid split hard at the vertical midpoint — cols 1-6 carry a single wall-filling typographic callout (discount tier, product category label, or urgency line) scaled to bleed top-to-bottom with zero top or bottom inset. Cols 7-12 are entirely consumed by a flush black hard block, edge-to-edge on three sides, holding secondary promo details — item scope, conditions, deadline — stacked in tight compressed left-aligned lines. No gutter between columns; the raw color boundary acts as the sole divider. Any micro-label such as a slide index or legal disclaimer sits bottom-right inside the black block at minimum legible scale.
